classification.difficultyReason: Combine equal base angles, supplementary angles and a diagonal splitting the trapezium into triangles.

inlines.text: . Angles at the same base in an isosceles trapezium are equal. Work out the size of each angle labelled with a letter.

spec.description: Unshaded isosceles trapezium with parallel horizontal bases, equal-leg ticks, four labelled interior angle arcs and a solid rightward base extension carrying the 140° exterior angle.
spec.mathematics: Equal angles at each base; exterior and interior angles at the lower-right vertex are supplementary; angles between parallel bases on each leg are supplementary. Coordinates are construction coordinates, not additional student givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}m&=180^\circ-140^\circ\\m&=40^\circ\\p&=40^\circ\\n&=180^\circ-40^\circ\\n&=140^\circ\\o&=140^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^\circ$. Angles at the same base of an isosceles trapezium are equal, and co-interior angles between parallel bases sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: Unshaded isosceles trapezium with parallel horizontal bases, equal-leg ticks and a diagonal from upper left to lower right. The upper-right angle is 115°. At lower right, 29° lies between the diagonal and right leg, while a lies between the diagonal and lower base. The remaining unknowns are b at lower left and c between the left leg and diagonal at upper left.
spec.mathematics: The lower-right whole angle is 65° by co-interior angles. Subtracting 29° gives a=36°. Equal base angles give b=65°. The lower triangle gives c=79°. Construction coordinates preserve these sectors without adding measurements to the diagram.
spec.answerVisibility: The question diagram contains 115°, 29°, a, b and c, with no supplied answer values.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}a+29^\circ+115^\circ&=180^\circ\\a+144^\circ&=180^\circ\\a&=36^\circ\end{align*}$
Co-interior angles between parallel bases sum to $180^\circ$.
$\begin{align*}b&=a+29^\circ\\b&=65^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles at the same base of an isosceles trapezium are equal.
$\begin{align*}c+36^\circ+65^\circ&=180^\circ\\c+101^\circ&=180^\circ\\c&=79^\circ\end{align*}$
Angles in the triangle below the diagonal sum to $180^\circ$.
